3.speaker: Symon Holl
3.text: “Even though I agree with your point Gus, this could be the best choice to handle this discreetly.”

4.speaker: Symon Holl
4.text: “We scheduled the construction to finish sooner but Taurus Holding might miss that target with the current trajectory.”

5.speaker: Gus Manger
5.text: “I don't support that bill just like you Mr. President. The reason is simple, I know it will cause issues with corporations and result in increased employee costs.”

6.speaker: Gus Manger
6.text: “There is little point in passing that bill late. Maybe the best way out of this is replacing the workers on strike.”

7.speaker: Gus Manger
7.text: “Rather than incompetence, according to their report, their expenses increased drastically due to the new bill increasing workers costs.”

9.speaker: Symon Holl
9.text: “However, following the veto, we have ceased the implementation of the policy and disbanded the expert team, resulting in a potential increase in the cost of the bill if new teams are to be established.”

11.speaker: Gus Manger
11.text: “Let's see what happens. If we miss the deadlines the people will lose faith in our capabilities.”

12.speaker: Player
12.text: “Let's enjoy the hospitality of the Mayor.”

13.speaker: Symon Holl
13.text: “I doubt sitting idly will help in this case.”

14.speaker: Gus Manger
14.text: “Let's hope this will be enough to have a timely opening.”

18.speaker: Symon Holl
18.text: “This will most likely cause a delay but Taurus Holding will be informed immediately.”

19.speaker: Symon Holl
19.text: “Well then. Thank you for coming. That is all on this matter.”

20.speaker: Symon Holl
20.text: “As you wish. I will allocate the funding to Taurus Holding.”

21.speaker: Symon Holl
21.text: “The strike that popped up at the construction site is causing issues.”

25.speaker: Symon Holl
25.text: “After the terrible Morbel mine disaster, workers have been on edge. Vetoing the Workers' Rights bill certainly did not help with the situation either.”

27.speaker: Symon Holl
27.text: “Strikers primary demand is for the bill to be reinstated. We have to solve the issue or the construction will stay halted longer.”

29.speaker: Player
29.text: “We don't have the funds to spare.”

30.speaker: Player
30.text: “Give them the additional funds.” [-1 Government Budget]

31.speaker: Symon Holl
31.text: “Taurus Holding has reached out to us and requested more funds.”

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: Symon nodded and we left the meeting room.

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “We could just wait it out until the strikers get tired.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “Why don't we just do what they want and pass the Workers' Rights bill?”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “Indeed we could just replace the striking workers.”

37.speaker: Symon Holl
37.text: “This will only serve to rile up the strikers even more. We might end up with a bigger mess.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “Why do they even need the extra money?”

39.speaker: Gus Manger
39.text: “And give in to the rabble? How many more strikes are going to create if we show them that they can change what the state has already decided on?”

41.speaker: Gus Manger
41.text: “This could work. I bet they will get tired after some time and go back to their jobs.”

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “It's important that we finish this project on time. Money is no matter.”

43.speaker: Gus Manger
43.text: “I think this is our best bet. We can't stand idle and we can't allow a few strikers to change the laws of the state.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Order Taurus Holding to replace the strikers with new workers. This should fix our issue.”

45.speaker: Narrator
45.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Vetoed"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedPeople"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn04_WorkersRights_Signed"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Vetoed"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Increase"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedPeople"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn04_WorkersRights_Signed"] == true) == false)

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “I'm not worried. Let's just wait it out. They will stop at one point and everything will be alright.”

47.speaker: Gus Manger
47.text: “Realities of running a business is to be able to adapt to changing circumstances. The most important thing here is to finish the project on time.”

49.speaker: Player
49.text: “We will begin the procedure to pass the vetoed Workers' Rights bill. [-2 Government Budget]”

50.speaker: Symon Holl
50.text: “We need to show people that we can finish this project, our first mega project, on time.”

51.speaker: Symon Holl
51.text: “They need it for unforeseen expenses that came from the new Workers' Rights Bill. A couple of shipment companies they had contracts with also increased costs on the necessary materials.”

52.speaker: Gus Manger
52.text: “It is unfortunate but construction can be disrupted when costs change dramatically. I knew that something was wrong when they offered the contract for cheaper. Underhall wouldn't have had this problem due to their wealth of experience.”

54.speaker: Symon Holl
54.text: “As per the report they have sent, to finish the railway on time, they realised more capital is necessary due to the new labour laws.”

55.speaker: Player
55.text: “Absolutely not. I will not let a few strikers decide the future of our country.”

57.speaker: Player
57.text: “We need to cut the head of the snake to truly stop this issue by replacing the strikers.”

58.speaker: Symon Holl
58.text: “I'm not sure about this but as you wish.”

59.speaker: Gus Manger
59.text: “Regardless, we might not have the choice if we want to finish this project on time.”

60.speaker: Symon Holl
60.text: “If we spend the extra amount they are requesting, we might miss other opportunities.”

61.speaker: Gus Manger
61.text: “I agree. If we let them change our laws on whim, this will lower the trust in our government and cause stability issues.”

62.speaker: Symon Holl
62.text: “Very well. Hopefully the backlash doesn't affect us too much.”

63.speaker: Gus Manger
63.text: “He does but we can't just let anyone change our laws after we sign them. What type of message does that send to the people? A weak government that backtracks on its decisions?”

64.speaker: Gus Manger
64.text: “If this causes a delay it would also cause us to lose face in-front of the eyes of the public. Sinking more money into Taurus isn't ideal either.”

65.speaker: Gus Manger
65.text: “Exactly. This is the only way to stop this from happening again. Make an example of the strikers so that no one else attempts it again.”

66.speaker: Gus Manger
66.text: “So, anyone can change the laws of Sordland by organising a little strike. Respect for the state will be undermined.”

69.speaker: Symon Holl
69.text: “They should've seen this coming. If they didn't, which is the case, that's incompetency.”

70.speaker: Symon Holl
70.text: “We scheduled the construction to finish sooner but Taurus Holding might miss that target with the current trajectory.”

71.speaker: Gus Manger
71.text: “On top of it, this will affect all the companies in Sordland causing them to pay extra money to their employees. This small matter shouldn't have affected the whole country.”

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: The main purpose of our visit was to solve construction issues that began to endanger the deadline.

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: The L-1 Railway construction created the perfect opportunity to visit the green technological nerve centre of Sordland. Dozens of electrical engineers from the city were part of the electrification upgrade of the rail track.

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: The Gelsord Research Council was very reluctant to let us use their facilities as the rectors weren't at all pleased by the reduction of education funding.

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: Symon looked a little more stressed than usual. Gus was also here to find solutions. He eyed me for a while.

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: The Gelsord Research Council was very willing to let us use their facilities because the rectors were pleased by the increase of the education funding.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: The Gelsord Research Council let us use their facilities, but the rectors weren't interested in our affairs.

92.speaker: Gus Manger
92.text: “One thing is for certain, our administration must avoid working with Taurus in the future and opt for safe choices like Underhall.”

95.speaker: Gus Manger
95.text: “True but we took an extra risk on this one. If something is too good to be true, it isn't. I had a bad feeling about the cheaper contract.”

96.speaker: Gus Manger
96.text: “There are people I know in the management of Underhall. They will be available for a second project in the future.”

97.speaker: Gus Manger
97.text: “The question is are we going to give Taurus the funds they requested.”

99.speaker: Gus Manger
99.text: “Not the fossil of a company. If anybody will have timeline issues it is them.”

120.speaker: Symon Holl
120.text: “As much as I hate to say it, I think passing the Workers' Rights bill might be our best bet.”
